title: Rust session navigation and terminal sheets
note: Paired clean native builds: base e9a07c5c53b473a739b2db9cd4d4c243c295fa13, candidate 74ff74e9d512949022bebf6398af7f0a8947eecc. Six standard/extended models, eight standard scenarios, three trials, medium thinking where available; DeepSeek uses its high default. This slice adds interactive session navigation and shared terminal sheets. The headless suite does not exercise session switching; compiled-provider and real-gateway fullscreen/inline PTY checks independently verify model/thinking/history restoration, log separation, cancellation and terminal restoration. No performance claim. The only flag is GPT failures 2 -> 4: the base succeeds in 22/24 tasks and the candidate in 20/24. All six failed samples report more than 2,000 trailing whitespace characters after tool arguments without a closing call, causing the existing guard to abort. The same failure class appears on both arms and in the preceding interactive-controls record. After normalizing executable and temporary paths, all 144 paired system prompts match; the six captured first-request pairs match except for prompt_cache_key in two models. This supports treating the failures as the existing provider-generation problem; it does not prove the extra candidate failures are unrelated. The flag is accepted for this opt-in UI/session slice because the protective guard is unchanged, no changed headless model input was found, and independent interactive checks pass. Provider reliability remains unresolved; failed samples are retained and no retry replaces them. All other models pass 24/24 on each arm, with no additional regression flags. The test-only completion-readiness follow-up 18fd5a21a3 leaves the evaluated Rust source and binary unchanged.

settings.effort: medium where the model offers it; DeepSeek runs at high, its default, having no medium

regressionRule: all tasks, per model: total tokens with the 95% interval above zero; requests up more than 10% with the 95% interval above zero; failures +2 or more; any tool-error increase
